rounds.text: CG-VAK Software & Exports Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a remarkably low P/E ratio of just 7.51x [E1] and a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.18x [E2], with alternative key ratios placing the P/B at an even cheaper 0.98x against a lofty sector benchmark of 7.35x [E7]. This valuation disconnect is underscored by an exceptional return on assets of 10.14%, contrasting sharply with a dismal sector benchmark of -40.72% [E8]. The long-term operating history demonstrates powerful compounding, evidenced by a 19% compounded sales growth rate [E14] and a stellar 29% compounded profit growth rate over a decade [E18]. Recent performance confirms a strong rebound, marked by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 20% [E21] that outpaces 1-year price growth by 61%, signaling that fundamentals are leading the business to outperform expectations [E57]. Conceded: [E5].

The surface-level cheapness of CG-VAK Software & Exports Ltd—highlighted by a P/E of 7.51 and a price-to-book of 1.18—masks a profound structural deceleration in the core business [E1, E2, E68]. While long-term historical metrics look respectable, growth has sharply stalled over the medium term, with compounded sales growth collapsing to a meager 2% over 3 years and compounded profit growth contracting by -3% over the same 3-year window [E16, E20]. This fundamental slowdown has heavily damaged market sentiment, leaving the stock languishing just 5% of the way up its 52-week range near its ₹ 150 low [E5]. Furthermore, earnings growth is actively decelerating as flagged by quantitative screens, signaling that recent trailing twelve-month profit recoveries may be fragile or unsustainable [E21, E68]. Conceded: the company maintains a solid 10-year compounded sales growth of 19% and a 10-year profit growth of 29% [E14, E18].

The bear misinterprets the multi-year deceleration as a permanent structural stall, ignoring the powerful inflection happening right now in the business [E16, E20, E21]. Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth slowed to 2% and 3-year profit growth contracted by -3% [E16, E20]. However, the business has decisively broken out of that past trough, delivering a compelling 20% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21]. That accelerating profit rebound dramatically outpaces the 1-year price growth by 61%, proving that the stock price has completely lagged the fundamental reality and created a massive disconnect [E57]. Trading at a meager P/E of 7.51 and a P/B of 0.98 against sector benchmarks as high as 7.35, the market is mispricing a company delivering a stellar 10.14% return on assets compared to a disastrous -40.72% sector average [E1, E7, E8]. Finally, pinning the valuation to its 52-week low ignores that this deep discount sits on top of a proven 10-year compounding engine featuring 19% sales growth and 29% profit growth [E5, E14, E18].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 20% [E21]. However, pointing to a short-term rebound ignores the severe multi-year structural deceleration embedded in the business, where 3-year compounded sales growth crawled to 2% and 3-year profits actually contracted by -3% [E16, E20]. The screen explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating, demonstrating that the recent TTM tick-up is an isolated bounce rather than a secure trend [E68]. Furthermore, the bull leans on the low 7.51 P/E and 0.98 P/B ratios as mispricing, but fails to account for why the stock is pinned at just 5% of its 52-week range [E1, E2, E5, E7]. Finally, citing a 10-year historical sales compounding rate of 19% is misleading when recent performance has ground to a near-halt, leaving the market fully justified in keeping the valuation compressed [E5, E14].
